summary:
The starting-pitcher category is bleeding across the board, and that's the story to build around today. All three ratings show SP cold, with R1 and R2 both cratering to 40% over the last 14 days (74-112, n=186) — a brutal 9.2-point drop from their 49% season baseline. R3 is only marginally better at 45% (84-102), still 5.7 points under water. Fade SP-driven picks regardless of which rating is attached. On the flip side, R1's bullpen and hitting categories are carrying the load — hitting is flagged hot at 55% (102-84, +5.3pts over the 50% baseline), and bullpen sits at the same 55% clip, though note the bullpen streak is 4L across all three ratings, so recent results haven't caught up to the underlying number yet. Runs is the steadiest performer, with all three ratings riding a 3W streak and hit rates 52-56% over the window.

Strong-play units tell a cautionary tale short-term: every rating is bleeding cash over the last 7 days (R1 -10.0u, R2 -10.0u, R3 -12.0u) and still underwater at 14 days, but the season totals remain strongly positive (R3 leads at +28.0u, 132-119, 53%), so this looks like variance, not signal decay — don't panic-fade strong plays based on the recent skid alone. For category combinations, trends+runs is the top play at 55.2% (211-171, n=382), and trends pairs well across the board, confirming trends as the most reliable anchor category today. On the team side, lean into TBR when the model likes them — 72% overall (23-9) and an elite 78% on strong plays (18-5, +22.0u), the best combination of volume and unit profit in the sheet. BOS (74%, n=34) and LAD strong plays (85%, 11-2, +14.0u) are the other clear green lights. Avoid HOU strong plays — 30% (3-7, -7.0u) is a clear red flag despite a respectable overall 62% pick rate.
